plugins.name: motta-statusline
plugins.description: Two-line status line: where the session runs, repo and branch links, git state with push state and the last commit, the branch's PR with CI, conflicts and review (toasts when they change), model and effort, a context bar with the auto-compact point, rate-limit bars with a pace tick (files, ctx, 5h and 7d open the panes of changes-drill, context-drill and usage-drill), a prompt-cache countdown, tokens and the generation rate. Under the prompt in the CLI, or as a band above it.

plugins.name: context-drill
plugins.description: A Context pane that drills into what fills the window, read when it opens, after each turn while it is shown and on Refresh (a local estimate, no request sent): the /context categories as a stacked bar with the auto-compact tick and what grew since you opened it, the fill per turn against the auto-compact point, turns left before it fires, cache health, the heaviest messages and tokens by tool, then the memory files, MCP tools by server, agents and skills, and the startup cost against your average; a footer compacts with a focus you pick. Every part is a setting. motta-statusline's ctx opens it; so does /context-drill.

plugins.name: changes-drill
plugins.description: A Changes pane that says which turn changed each file and who (Claude, a subagent, Claude's shell or you), against HEAD, the session's start, the last turn or the base branch, with a guard for sensitive or out-of-scope files, the last two turns open and older ones folded, hover cards, and a History section of what happened, with a Branches button that opens branch-drill. Read-only, no model calls, no network. motta-statusline's files opens it; so does /changes-drill.

plugins.name: branch-drill
plugins.description: A Branches pane on top of changes-drill: Me (your branch against main, or where your work sits) and All (every branch as lanes or a subway map), each with a picker and hover cards; a commit opens its files. Opened from the Changes pane's Branches button or /branch-drill. Read-only, local git only, no model calls.

plugins.name: usage-drill
plugins.description: A Usage pane: each rate limit (5h, 7d) as motta-statusline's bar with a verdict; its readings, burn rate, budget, cost per turn, past windows, a GitHub-style activity grid and the spend by model. Toasts at thresholds. No request sent. motta-statusline's 5h and 7d open it; so does /usage-drill.

plugins.name: assumption-check
plugins.description: A side pane of the assumptions Claude makes, one dropdown per prompt, with counts that filter: mark one right, or wrong (type the fix or let Claude ask), ask why, open its source, or delete it. On from the start, /assumption-check off to stop; nothing in the pane reaches Claude unless you press wrong or why.

plugins.name: prompt-enhancer
plugins.description: /enhance <text> opens an Enhance pane that rewrites your draft one of two ways, in one model call: Cleaned up (a cheap model fixes typos, fillers, voice-to-text artifacts and punctuation, nothing else) or Expanded (written with the conversation: the outcome behind the draft, what a top practitioner would do, the task as verbs with techniques from other fields and an adversary, and how to verify it, rewritten as a prompt that asks for exactly that). Use it, send it or copy it.

plugins.name: emotive-spinner
plugins.description: The spinner line says what Claude is doing instead of a whimsical word: a symbol and plain words for the file it reads or writes (with its size, lines so far while it streams), the command it runs in its own description, the search, the page, the agents and what the latest is doing, thinking, writing the answer, or waiting for you. Read from the engine's events; no model calls. Terminal and desktop app.

plugins.name: tool-borders
plugins.description: Marks each tool call with a color: the hue says what it does (read, change, delegate, run, bookkeeping) and the shade how far it reaches (project, elsewhere on this machine, internet). A border in the CLI, a thin bar on the desktop app. The stroke says how it got past the permission check: a rule, the auto-mode classifier, you, or a refusal.

plugins.name: turn-receipt
plugins.description: A receipt under each turn's reply, yours and the ones agents' reports start: time, agents, edits, errors and cost added, colored; agents and edits open their panes. No model calls.

plugins.name: filetree
plugins.description: IDE-style file tree with git status that shimmers on files Claude reads and writes, and lists those outside its folder. Vendored from data-goblin/claude-code-filetree@bf8de32 (MIT).

plugins.name: savvy-progress
plugins.description: Live agents panel (/agents-info) with each subagent's model, context, cost and time, under a timeline of your turns: a session ruler in clock time with idle time folded, and one batch of lanes per turn. Vendored from JohnnyVizz/claude-kit@272a877 (MIT).

plugins.name: agent-lane
plugins.description: Skills for the agent lane: /motta-setup-repo sets a repo up for it (dev -> main flow, labels, delivery board, BOARD.md, forms, PR template, CI, ship workflow and scripts, AGENTS.md) from the templates it carries, /motta-intake turns notes into spike issues, /motta-settle-spike turns the owner's decisions into agent-ready issues, /motta-dispatch starts a worktree build session per ready issue, motta-build-issue builds one unattended to a PR with CI green, /motta-review acts on and answers the comments on agent: review issues and PRs, and /motta-ship-pr merges agent: human-approved PRs through the repo's gate script. They work in whichever repo they run in, following its .github/BOARD.md, and stop in a checkout that has none.

plugins.name: motta-heavydev
plugins.description: /motta-heavydev <issue>: a multi-agent flow for large changes in any repo. An intent interview, conservative and bold architects under an adversarial critic, an audit by the strongest model, then implementation, a diff review, QA against the running system and a PR, with a budget in API-equivalent dollars. Brings its seven hd-* agent types. Playbooks and run artifacts go to a store repo (vtex-copilot/motta-heavydev by default; store in ~/.claude/motta-heavydev.json changes it).
